data.content_ref: inline:SRC_005 depends on the thermal-mass storage mechanism detailed in SRC_003: the SVF-based radiative trap described in SRC_005 cannot produce a nocturnal temperature differential unless there is stored sensible heat in urban materials to be trapped. The SVF mechanism acts as a boundary condition on the release-rate of the stored heat, not as a standalone heat source. This dependence is REFUTED IF nocturnal UHI is observed in cities built entirely of low-thermal-mass materials (e.g., wood, fabric, light metal) where daytime heat storage is negligible—under that condition, if a UHI persists, SVF trapping must be operating on anthropogenic or advected heat, breaking the direct dependence on the SRC_003 storage mechanism.
